prompt:
Build a Simulink model of a rear-wheel-drive vehicle handling plant. The model shall contain coupled steering kinematics, dynamic wheel rotation, longitudinal and lateral tyre slip, nonlinear combined tyre-force generation, axle/body load transfer or equivalent force coupling, and longitudinal, lateral, and yaw vehicle dynamics. Rear-left and rear-right wheel torques shall act through the wheel and tyre dynamics; do not prescribe vehicle motion or slip outputs directly.

This task is an open-loop plant construction problem. It does not require a yaw-rate feedback controller. A desired-yaw-rate diagnostic may be computed from the commanded steering and measured vehicle state, but it must not be presented as evidence of closed-loop torque-vectoring control.

Read the scalar workspace inputs steering_angle_deg, rear_left_torque_nm, and rear_right_torque_nm. Support steering_angle_deg from -6 to +6 degrees and each rear-wheel torque from 15 to 45 N*m. The model shall remain finite for equal rear torques, changes in the equal-torque level, and small mirrored left/right torque differences at fixed total torque. Simulate for 5 seconds and save the final model as cand_XAUTO10.slx.

Record complete finite Timeseries from 0 to 5 seconds in the following containers. vehicle_motion_state shall have seven columns in this order: longitudinal velocity (m/s), lateral velocity (m/s), longitudinal acceleration (m/s^2), lateral acceleration (m/s^2), yaw rate (rad/s), yaw acceleration (rad/s^2), and desired-yaw-rate diagnostic (rad/s). wheel_slip_state shall have twelve columns: four longitudinal-slip channels, four lateral-slip channels, and four combined-slip channels, each ordered front-left, front-right, rear-left, rear-right. rear_wheel_command_state shall have three columns: steering command (deg), rear-left torque command (N*m), and rear-right torque command (N*m). All three time vectors shall be strictly increasing and cover the full run.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XAUTO10.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
